HOMEOWNERS POLICY FORM HF-8 — EXCERPTS, ENDORSEMENTS AND CLAIM FILE CLM-8922960
Extract assembled for the coverage decision. Pagination removed. Notes in square brackets were added by the file clerk.

======================================================================
PART A — POLICY DECLARATIONS (TERM IN FORCE)
======================================================================
Policyholder: Hiro Hoffmann
Policy number: HP-70329669
Form: HF-8 (edition 01/2024)
Term: 19 December 2025 to 19 December 2026
Deductible: $2,500 per occurrence

======================================================================
PART B — DEFINITIONS
======================================================================
1. 'Vacant' means that the dwelling contains no furnishings or contents sufficient for normal residential use and no one has lived in it for more than 30 consecutive days.
2. 'Unoccupied' means that the dwelling contains furnishings sufficient for normal residential use but no one has lived in it for more than 30 consecutive days. An unoccupied dwelling is not vacant.
3. 'Repeated seepage or leakage' means water or steam escaping continuously or repeatedly for 10 days or longer.
4. 'Concealed water' means water that escapes within walls, floors, ceilings or under a slab, that is not visible from any living space, and whose escape is unknown to the insured until discovery.
5. 'Sudden and accidental discharge' means an escape of water that begins abruptly and is not repeated seepage or leakage.
6. 'Residence premises' means the one- or two-family dwelling where the insured resides, shown in the declarations, including structures attached to it.

======================================================================
PART C — COVERAGES
======================================================================
2.1. Fungi and rot. We pay up to $10,000 for the removal of fungi, wet or dry rot resulting from a covered loss, including the cost of testing the air and property.
2.2. Debris removal. We will pay the reasonable expense of removing debris of covered property after a covered loss, up to 5% of the limit that applies to the damaged property, as an additional amount of insurance.
2.3. Emergency mitigation. Where water has escaped, the insured must arrange drying and dehumidification within 72 hours of discovery; the cost is covered as part of the loss up to $10,000.
2.4. Pair or set. In case of loss to a pair or set we may elect to repair or replace any part to restore the pair or set to its value before the loss, or to pay the difference between actual cash value before and after the loss.
2.5. Insuring agreement. We will pay for direct physical loss to covered property caused by a peril insured against, unless the loss is excluded or limited in this contract. The most we will pay for any one occurrence is the applicable limit shown in the declarations, less the deductible.
2.6. Loss settlement. Losses are settled at the cost to repair or replace with materials of like kind and quality, without deduction for depreciation, provided repair or replacement is completed within 180 days of the loss; otherwise on an actual cash value basis until completion.

======================================================================
PART D — GENERAL CONDITIONS
======================================================================
3.1. Intentional loss. We do not cover loss caused by an act that the insured committed, or directed someone else to commit, intending the loss to happen.
3.2. Governmental action. We do not cover the destruction, confiscation or seizure of property by order of any governmental or public authority, except as ordered to prevent the spread of fire.
3.3. Suit against us. No action can be brought against us unless there has been full compliance with all of the terms of this contract and the action is started within 3 years after the date of loss.
3.4. Definitions of general application. In this contract 'we' and 'us' mean the insurer that issued it, and 'you' means the insured shown on the declarations page. 'Business day' means a day other than Saturday, Sunday or a public holiday at the place shown in the declarations.
3.5. Subrogation. Any party covered under this contract may be required to assign to us rights of recovery against another party, up to the amount we have paid. The covered party must do nothing after loss to impair those rights.
3.6. Volunteer payments. We will not pay for any expense voluntarily incurred by the insured beyond $500 without our prior agreement, except for emergency measures reasonably necessary to protect the property from further loss.
3.7. Other insurance. If a loss covered by this contract is also covered by other insurance, we will pay only the proportion of the loss that the limit of liability that applies under this contract bears to the total amount of insurance covering the loss.
3.8. Nuclear hazard. We do not cover loss caused directly or indirectly by nuclear reaction, radiation or radioactive contamination, whether controlled or uncontrolled, and whether or not caused by a peril otherwise covered.
3.9. Inflation guard. The limits shown in the declarations increase by 2% at each anniversary of the inception date unless this endorsement is deleted by the insured.
3.10. Cancellation. The insured may cancel at any time by returning the contract to us or by notifying us in writing of the date cancellation is to take effect. We may cancel by mailing notice at least 30 days before the effective date, or 30 days where the cancellation is for reasons other than non-payment. Unearned premium is refunded pro rata.

======================================================================
PART E — EXCLUSIONS (SECTION 4) AND SUBLIMITS
======================================================================
4.1. Earth movement, including earthquake, landslide, mudflow, sinkhole, subsidence, or earth sinking, rising or shifting, whether caused by or resulting from human or animal forces or any act of nature.
4.2. Water from flood, surface water, waves, tidal water, or overflow of a body of water, or spray from any of these, whether or not driven by wind; water that backs up through sewers or drains except as provided by endorsement.
4.3. Water or steam that seeps or leaks repeatedly out of plumbing, heating or cooling equipment, a fire sprinkler installation, or a domestic appliance. Exception 4.3.1: this exclusion does not apply to concealed water, in which case we will pay for the resulting damage to the building subject to the concealed-water sublimit shown in Part D, less the deductible. Exception 4.3.1 does not apply if the insured knew of the seepage or leakage before the damage was discovered.
4.4. Wear and tear, marring, deterioration, mechanical breakdown, rust or other corrosion, mould, wet or dry rot, or smog, except that resulting ensuing loss from a covered peril is covered.
4.5. Freezing of plumbing, heating or cooling equipment, a fire sprinkler installation, or a domestic appliance, unless the insured took reasonable care to keep the building heated, or turned off the water and drained the pipes.
4.6. Theft in or to a dwelling under construction, or of materials and supplies for use in the construction, until the dwelling is finished and occupied.
4.7. Vacancy: loss to the building caused by water, freezing, vandalism, glass breakage or theft while the dwelling is vacant. Exception 4.7.1: this exclusion does not apply while the dwelling is undergoing renovation under a building permit issued by the local authority. This exclusion does not apply to an unoccupied dwelling.
4.8. Power failure that originates off the residence premises, unless a covered peril ensues on the premises and then only for the ensuing loss.
4.9. Intentional loss, neglect, war, nuclear hazard and governmental action as set out in Part E.
Sublimits (Part E): concealed water $7,500 per occurrence; mould remediation $5,000; trees, shrubs and plants $500 per item.

======================================================================
PART F — ADDITIONAL CONDITIONS
======================================================================
5.1. Territorial limits. Coverage applies to losses occurring within the territory shown in the declarations. Property temporarily removed from the premises is covered for up to 10% of the applicable limit, but not for more than 45 consecutive days.
5.2. War. We do not cover loss caused by war, including undeclared war, civil war, insurrection, rebellion or revolution, or by warlike acts of a military force or personnel.
5.3. Electronic data. Loss of or damage to electronic data is covered only for the cost of blank media and the cost of copying from backups, subject to a limit of $5,000 per occurrence.
5.4. Mortgagee clause. If a mortgagee is named in the declarations, any loss payable under Coverage A is paid to the mortgagee and the insured as interests appear. Denial of the insured's claim does not apply to a valid claim of the mortgagee if the mortgagee notifies us of any change in ownership, occupancy or substantial change in risk of which it is aware.
5.5. Concealment or fraud. We do not provide coverage if, whether before or after a loss, the insured has intentionally concealed or misrepresented any material fact or circumstance, engaged in fraudulent conduct, or made false statements relating to this contract.
5.6. Neglect. We do not cover loss that results from the insured failing to take reasonable steps to protect and preserve the property once a loss has occurred.
5.7. Loss payment. We will adjust all losses with the insured and pay within 30 days after we reach agreement, after entry of a final judgment, or after the filing of an appraisal award with us, whichever comes first.
5.8. Appraisal. If the parties fail to agree on the amount of loss, either may demand an appraisal. Each party selects a competent appraiser within 30 days; the appraisers select an umpire. A decision agreed to by any two is binding. Each party pays its own appraiser and shares the cost of the umpire equally.
5.9. Ordinance or law. Extra cost caused by having to comply with building codes or other regulations when repairing, rebuilding or demolishing is covered up to 10% of the Coverage A limit.
5.10. Waiver or change of provisions. A waiver or change of a provision of this contract must be in writing by us to be valid. Our request for an appraisal or examination does not waive any of our rights.

======================================================================
PART G — ENDORSEMENTS ON FILE
======================================================================
ENDORSEMENT HE-8090 — CONCEALED WATER SUBLIMIT INCREASE. For policy terms renewed or issued on or after 24 December 2025, the concealed-water sublimit in Part D is $10,000 instead of $7,500. All other terms unchanged. [clerk: attached to the file at renewal]

======================================================================
PART H — CLAIM FILE CLM-8922960
======================================================================
Claim CLM-8922960. Insured: Hiro Hoffmann. Residence premises: 303 Birch Way, Cape Town. Date of loss (discovery): 8 May 2026.
Current term: renewed effective 19 December 2025, expiring 19 December 2026. Deductible $2,500. Coverage A limit $410,000.
Adjuster's narrative (Zofia Coetzee): The insured returned from a stay with family after 25 consecutive days away. The house remained fully furnished with the insured's contents in place. On return the insured found water damage to the hallway subfloor. The plumber traced the source to a split flexible hose under the kitchen sink, in plain view. From the extent of staining and the plumber's report the leak had been running for about 9 days before discovery. The insured states that a damp smell had been noticed and reported to the letting agent before the absence.
Repair estimate (building): $13,000. Contents claim: none.
[Trainee note, Bram Jansen: burst pipe, covered peril, pay the estimate $13,000 less $2,500 deductible.]
[File correspondence, extracted]
From Kalinda Iversen to Orla Abara, 18 September 2025: Please find attached the contractor's invoice and the photographs for CLM-8922960. The customer asks whether a further claim can be added later; I have told them a separate form is needed. Can you confirm the figures shown on the declarations are the current ones?
From Orla Abara to Kalinda Iversen, 20 September 2025: Confirmed. Note that the customer's broker has asked to be copied on the outcome letter. Please also check whether any endorsement or amendment on the file changes the figures before we draft the letter; the base text alone is not the whole story.
From Kalinda Iversen to Orla Abara, 26 September 2025: Draft outcome letter to follow once the position is settled. The trainee has added a note with a recommendation; it has not been reviewed.

question.instructions: How should claim CLM-8922960 for the building water damage be decided under the policy as it stands?

criteria.deny_vacant_dwelling: Deny: the vacancy exclusion (4.7) bars the building water damage and no exception restores cover.
criteria.deny_repeated_leakage: Deny: the repeated-seepage exclusion (4.3) bars the loss and the concealed-water exception does not restore it.
criteria.pay_within_7500_sublimit: Pay: cover is restored by the concealed-water exception, capped at $7,500 after the deductible.
criteria.pay_within_10000_sublimit: Pay: cover is restored by the concealed-water exception, capped at $10,000 after the deductible.
criteria.pay_estimate_less_deductible: Pay in full: no exclusion or sublimit applies; the repair estimate minus the deductible is payable.

rationale: (1) The dwelling was furnished and empty for 25 days (not more than 30), so it was neither vacant nor unoccupied under the definitions. (2) The vacancy exclusion does not apply. (3) 9 days is less than 10 days, so the water is not 'repeated seepage or leakage'. (4) Decision: sudden discharge, covered in full less the deductible: $10,500.

1.1. Uptime calculation. Monthly uptime percentage = (available minutes) / (total minutes in the month minus excluded minutes) x 100, rounded to three decimals.

1.3. Customer-caused outages. Minutes of unavailability caused by the customer's own equipment, credentials or configuration are not counted as downtime but remain in the denominator.
1.4. Scheduled maintenance outside the window. Maintenance performed outside the published window counts as downtime in full.
1.5. Service credit schedule (original): monthly uptime at or above 99.9%: no credit; at or above 99.5% but below 99.9%: 5% of the monthly fee; at or above 99.0% but below 99.5%: 10%; below 99.0%: 25%.
1.6. Claims. Credits must be claimed in writing within 30 days after the end of the month and are applied to the next invoice.

======================================================================

======================================================================

2.2. Maintenance notices. Scheduled maintenance is announced at least 72 hours in advance through the status page. Maintenance that starts inside the window but runs beyond it counts as downtime for the minutes outside the window.

2.6. Data handling. The provider processes customer data only as instructed and in accordance with the data processing schedule. Backups are retained for 90 days.
2.7. Reporting. A monthly service report is issued within 7 business days after the month end and contains the incident log, the uptime calculation and any credit due.
2.8. Force majeure. Neither party is liable for delay or failure caused by events beyond its reasonable control, including natural disasters, war, and failures of public networks, provided the affected party notifies the other promptly.
2.9. Termination for chronic failure. If the uptime falls into the 25% credit tier in any three months of a rolling six-month period, the customer may terminate the affected service on 45 days' notice without penalty.

======================================================================

question.instructions: Is any part of the building water damage in claim CLM-4781148 payable under the policy?

criteria.true: Some amount is payable (with or without a sublimit).
criteria.false: The claim is excluded and nothing is payable.

rationale: (1) The dwelling was without furnishings and empty for 90 days (more than 45), so it was vacant under the definitions. (2) The vacancy exclusion applies. ======================================================================
SECTION 1 — PURPOSE AND SCOPE
======================================================================
This policy sets out when Copperleaf Systems reimburses relocation costs for employees who move at the company's request. It applies to all grades and locations.

======================================================================
SECTION 2 — RULES
======================================================================
1. Eligibility (distance test). A relocation is eligible only if the one-way distance from the employee's former home to the new workplace exceeds the distance from the former home to the former workplace by at least 60 km.
2. Time limit. Claims must be submitted with receipts within 120 days of the employee's start date at the new workplace. Where the employee is on approved leave during that period, the limit is extended by the number of leave days.
3. Caps. Reimbursement is capped by grade: G1 $4,000; G2 $7,500; G3 $10,000. Amounts above the cap are not reimbursed.
4. Dependants supplement. Where a spouse, partner or dependent child moves with the employee, the cap is increased by $1,500.
5. Excluded costs. Costs of buying or selling a home, mortgage penalties, and temporary accommodation beyond 30 nights are not reimbursable under this policy.
6. Repayment. An employee who leaves the company within 12 months of the start date must repay the reimbursement pro rata.

======================================================================
SECTION 3 — PROCESS
======================================================================
3.1. Interaction with other policies. Travel on the move day is reimbursed under this policy, not under the travel policy. Costs reimbursed under this policy are not claimable again under any other policy.
3.2. Advances. An advance of up to 50% of the applicable cap may be requested before the move; it is deducted from the final reimbursement. Unused advances must be repaid within 30 days.
3.3. Approvals. A relocation must be approved in writing by the receiving manager and by HR (Tomasz Tremblay's team) before the move date. Approval is recorded on form RL-80 and attached to the employee's file.
3.4. Tax treatment. Reimbursements are reported in accordance with local tax rules. Where a reimbursement is taxable, the amount paid to the employee is not grossed up unless the offer letter says otherwise.
3.5. Appeals. An employee may appeal a decision under this policy within 10 business days by writing to the HR director. The appeal is decided within 30 days; the decision on appeal is final.
3.6. Audit. Internal audit samples 5% of relocation claims each year. A claim found to be inaccurate may be recovered from salary in accordance with the deductions policy.
3.7. Data protection. Documents submitted with a claim are kept for 5 years after the claim is closed and are accessible only to HR and to the auditors.
3.8. Definitions. 'Start date' means the first day the employee is required to attend the new workplace, as stated in the transfer letter. 'Former home' means the address on file on the date of the transfer letter.
3.9. Receipts. Only itemised receipts in the employee's name are accepted. Credit-card statements alone are not sufficient. Receipts in a foreign currency are converted at the company's monthly rate for the month of the expense.

======================================================================
SECTION 4 — GENERAL PROVISIONS
======================================================================
4.1. Suit against us. No action can be brought against us unless there has been full compliance with all of the terms of this contract and the action is started within 2 years after the date of loss.
4.2. Salvage. When we pay for a loss we may take all or part of the damaged property at an agreed or appraised value. There is no abandonment of property to us.
4.3. Other insurance. If a loss covered by this contract is also covered by other insurance, we will pay only the proportion of the loss that the limit of liability that applies under this contract bears to the total amount of insurance covering the loss.

Denial of the employee's claim does not apply to a valid claim of the mortgagee if the mortgagee notifies us of any change in ownership, occupancy or substantial change in risk of which it is aware.
4.5. Governmental action. We do not cover the destruction, confiscation or seizure of property by order of any governmental or public authority, except as ordered to prevent the spread of fire.

4.7. Territorial limits. Coverage applies to losses occurring within the territory shown in the declarations. Property temporarily removed from the premises is covered for up to 15% of the applicable limit, but not for more than 60 consecutive days.
4.8. Subrogation. Any party covered under this contract may be required to assign to us rights of recovery against another party, up to the amount we have paid. The covered party must do nothing after loss to impair those rights.
4.9. Ordinance or law. Extra cost caused by having to comply with building codes or other regulations when repairing, rebuilding or demolishing is covered up to 15% of the Coverage A limit.

======================================================================

======================================================================
SECTION 1 — PURPOSE AND SCOPE
======================================================================
This policy sets out when Oakhaven Systems reimburses relocation costs for employees who move at the company's request. It applies to all grades and locations.

======================================================================
SECTION 2 — RULES
======================================================================
1. Eligibility (distance test). A relocation is eligible only if the one-way distance from the employee's former home to the new workplace exceeds the distance from the former home to the former workplace by at least 60 km.
2. Time limit. Claims must be submitted with receipts within 90 days of the employee's start date at the new workplace. Where the employee is on approved leave during that period, the limit is extended by the number of leave days.
3. Caps. Reimbursement is capped by grade: G1 $4,000; G2 $7,500; G3 $10,000. Amounts above the cap are not reimbursed.
4. Dependants supplement. Where a spouse, partner or dependent child moves with the employee, the cap is increased by $1,500.
5. Excluded costs. Costs of buying or selling a home, mortgage penalties, and temporary accommodation beyond 30 nights are not reimbursable under this policy.
6. Repayment. An employee who leaves the company within 12 months of the start date must repay the reimbursement pro rata.

======================================================================
SECTION 3 — PROCESS
======================================================================
3.1. Appeals. An employee may appeal a decision under this policy within 5 business days by writing to the HR director. The appeal is decided within 20 days; the decision on appeal is final.
3.2. Approvals. A relocation must be approved in writing by the receiving manager and by HR (Milena Abara's team) before the move date. Approval is recorded on form RL-54 and attached to the employee's file.
3.3. Interaction with other policies. Travel on the move day is reimbursed under this policy, not under the travel policy. Costs reimbursed under this policy are not claimable again under any other policy.
3.4. Receipts. Only itemised receipts in the employee's name are accepted. Credit-card statements alone are not sufficient. Receipts in a foreign currency are converted at the company's monthly rate for the month of the expense.
3.5. Audit. Internal audit samples 10% of relocation claims each year. A claim found to be inaccurate may be recovered from salary in accordance with the deductions policy.
3.6. Temporary accommodation. Where temporary accommodation is reimbursed, the employee must move to permanent accommodation within 30 nights; extensions require the approval of the HR director.
3.7. Tax treatment. Reimbursements are reported in accordance with local tax rules. Where a reimbursement is taxable, the amount paid to the employee is not grossed up unless the offer letter says otherwise.
3.8. Advances. An advance of up to 50% of the applicable cap may be requested before the move; it is deducted from the final reimbursement. Unused advances must be repaid within 20 days.
3.9. Data protection. Documents submitted with a claim are kept for 5 years after the claim is closed and are accessible only to HR and to the auditors.

======================================================================
SECTION 4 — GENERAL PROVISIONS
======================================================================
4.1. Subrogation. Any party covered under this contract may be required to assign to us rights of recovery against another party, up to the amount we have paid. The covered party must do nothing after loss to impair those rights.
4.2. Appraisal. If the parties fail to agree on the amount of loss, either may demand an appraisal. Each party selects a competent appraiser within 14 days; the appraisers select an umpire. A decision agreed to by any two is binding. Each party pays its own appraiser and shares the cost of the umpire equally.
4.3. Neglect. We do not cover loss that results from the employee failing to take reasonable steps to protect and preserve the property once a loss has occurred.
4.4. Volunteer payments. We will not pay for any expense voluntarily incurred by the employee beyond $2,500 without our prior agreement, except for emergency measures reasonably necessary to protect the property from further loss.
4.5. Other insurance. If a loss covered by this contract is also covered by other insurance, we will pay only the proportion of the loss that the limit of liability that applies under this contract bears to the total amount of insurance covering the loss.
4.6. Territorial limits. Coverage applies to losses occurring within the territory shown in the declarations. Property temporarily removed from the premises is covered for up to 10% of the applicable limit, but not for more than 60 consecutive days.
4.7. Suit against us. No action can be brought against us unless there has been full compliance with all of the terms of this contract and the action is started within 3 years after the date of loss.
4.8. Assignment. Assignment of this contract is not valid unless we give our written consent.
4.9. Concealment or fraud. We do not provide coverage if, whether before or after a loss, the employee has intentionally concealed or misrepresented any material fact or circumstance, engaged in fraudulent conduct, or made false statements relating to this contract.
4.10. Definitions of general application. In this contract 'we' and 'us' mean the insurer that issued it, and 'you' means the employee shown on the declarations page. 'Business day' means a day other than Saturday, Sunday or a public holiday at the place shown in the declarations.

SECTION 1 — PURPOSE AND SCOPE
======================================================================
This policy sets out when Copperleaf Systems reimburses relocation costs for employees who move at the company's request. It applies to all grades and locations.

======================================================================
SECTION 2 — RULES
======================================================================
1. Eligibility (distance test). A relocation is eligible only if the one-way distance from the employee's former home to the new workplace exceeds the distance from the former home to the former workplace by at least 40 km.
2. Time limit. Claims must be submitted with receipts within 120 days of the employee's start date at the new workplace. Where the employee is on approved leave during that period, the limit is extended by the number of leave days.
3. Caps. Reimbursement is capped by grade: G1 $4,000; G2 $7,500; G3 $10,000. Amounts above the cap are not reimbursed.
4. Dependants supplement. Where a spouse, partner or dependent child moves with the employee, the cap is increased by $1,000.
5. Excluded costs. Costs of buying or selling a home, mortgage penalties, and temporary accommodation beyond 30 nights are not reimbursable under this policy.
6. Repayment. An employee who leaves the company within 12 months of the start date must repay the reimbursement pro rata.

======================================================================
SECTION 3 — PROCESS
======================================================================
3.1. Appeals. An employee may appeal a decision under this policy within 15 business days by writing to the HR director. The appeal is decided within 30 days; the decision on appeal is final.
3.2. Audit. Internal audit samples 5% of relocation claims each year. A claim found to be inaccurate may be recovered from salary in accordance with the deductions policy.
3.3. Definitions. 'Start date' means the first day the employee is required to attend the new workplace, as stated in the transfer letter. 'Former home' means the address on file on the date of the transfer letter.
3.4. Approvals. A relocation must be approved in writing by the receiving manager and by HR (Katja Sandoval's team) before the move date. Approval is recorded on form RL-55 and attached to the employee's file.
3.5. Temporary accommodation. Where temporary accommodation is reimbursed, the employee must move to permanent accommodation within 30 nights; extensions require the approval of the HR director.
3.6. Advances. An advance of up to 50% of the applicable cap may be requested before the move; it is deducted from the final reimbursement. Unused advances must be repaid within 30 days.
3.7. Data protection. Documents submitted with a claim are kept for 5 years after the claim is closed and are accessible only to HR and to the auditors.
3.8. Receipts. Only itemised receipts in the employee's name are accepted. Credit-card statements alone are not sufficient. Receipts in a foreign currency are converted at the company's monthly rate for the month of the expense.
3.9. Tax treatment. Reimbursements are reported in accordance with local tax rules. Where a reimbursement is taxable, the amount paid to the employee is not grossed up unless the offer letter says otherwise.
3.10. Interaction with other policies. Travel on the move day is reimbursed under this policy, not under the travel policy. Costs reimbursed under this policy are not claimable again under any other policy.

======================================================================
SECTION 4 — GENERAL PROVISIONS
======================================================================
4.1. Inflation guard. The limits shown in the declarations increase by 2% at each anniversary of the inception date unless this endorsement is deleted by the employee.
4.2. Other insurance. If a loss covered by this contract is also covered by other insurance, we will pay only the proportion of the loss that the limit of liability that applies under this contract bears to the total amount of insurance covering the loss.
4.3. Mortgagee clause. If a mortgagee is named in the declarations, any loss payable under Coverage A is paid to the mortgagee and the employee as interests appear. 4.5. Electronic data. Loss of or damage to electronic data is covered only for the cost of blank media and the cost of copying from backups, subject to a limit of $5,000 per occurrence.
4.6. Volunteer payments. We will not pay for any expense voluntarily incurred by the employee beyond $250 without our prior agreement, except for emergency measures reasonably necessary to protect the property from further loss.
4.7. Intentional loss. We do not cover loss caused by an act that the employee committed, or directed someone else to commit, intending the loss to happen.
4.8. Concealment or fraud. We do not provide coverage if, whether before or after a loss, the employee has intentionally concealed or misrepresented any material fact or circumstance, engaged in fraudulent conduct, or made false statements relating to this contract.
4.9. Nuclear hazard. We do not cover loss caused directly or indirectly by nuclear reaction, radiation or radioactive contamination, whether controlled or uncontrolled, and whether or not caused by a peril otherwise covered.
4.10. Assignment. Assignment of this contract is not valid unless we give our written consent.

======================================================================
SECTION 5 — AMENDMENTS
======================================================================
AMENDMENT A-77 (effective 7 November 2025): for relocations where the employee's start date at the new workplace is on or after the effective date, the caps in rule 3 are increased to G1 $5,000; G2 $8,500; G3 $11,000. Relocations with earlier start dates remain on the previous caps.

SECTION 6 — CASE FILE REL-671214
======================================================================

Distances (from the former home, one way, per the routing tool): to former workplace 28 km; to new workplace 68 km.

This policy sets out when Quarry Energy reimburses relocation costs for employees who move at the company's request. It applies to all grades and locations.

======================================================================

======================================================================
1. Eligibility (distance test). A relocation is eligible only if the one-way distance from the employee's former home to the new workplace exceeds the distance from the former home to the former workplace by at least 40 km.
2. Time limit. Claims must be submitted with receipts within 120 days of the employee's start date at the new workplace. Where the employee is on approved leave during that period, the limit is extended by the number of leave days.
3. Caps. Reimbursement is capped by grade: G1 $3,000; G2 $6,000; G3 $12,000. Amounts above the cap are not reimbursed.
4. Dependants supplement. Where a spouse, partner or dependent child moves with the employee, the cap is increased by $2,000.
5. Excluded costs. Costs of buying or selling a home, mortgage penalties, and temporary accommodation beyond 30 nights are not reimbursable under this policy.
6. Repayment. An employee who leaves the company within 12 months of the start date must repay the reimbursement pro rata.

======================================================================
SECTION 3 — PROCESS
======================================================================
3.1. Advances. An advance of up to 50% of the applicable cap may be requested before the move; it is deducted from the final reimbursement. Unused advances must be repaid within 30 days.
3.2. Receipts. Only itemised receipts in the employee's name are accepted. Credit-card statements alone are not sufficient. Receipts in a foreign currency are converted at the company's monthly rate for the month of the expense.
3.3. Temporary accommodation. Where temporary accommodation is reimbursed, the employee must move to permanent accommodation within 30 nights; extensions require the approval of the HR director.
3.4. Interaction with other policies. Travel on the move day is reimbursed under this policy, not under the travel policy. Costs reimbursed under this policy are not claimable again under any other policy.
3.5. Definitions. 'Start date' means the first day the employee is required to attend the new workplace, as stated in the transfer letter. 'Former home' means the address on file on the date of the transfer letter.
3.6. Approvals. A relocation must be approved in writing by the receiving manager and by HR (Farid Bakker's team) before the move date. Approval is recorded on form RL-75 and attached to the employee's file.
3.7. Tax treatment. Reimbursements are reported in accordance with local tax rules. Where a reimbursement is taxable, the amount paid to the employee is not grossed up unless the offer letter says otherwise.
3.8. Appeals. An employee may appeal a decision under this policy within 15 business days by writing to the HR director. The appeal is decided within 30 days; the decision on appeal is final.
3.9. Data protection. Documents submitted with a claim are kept for 7 years after the claim is closed and are accessible only to HR and to the auditors.

======================================================================
SECTION 4 — GENERAL PROVISIONS
======================================================================
4.1. Volunteer payments. We will not pay for any expense voluntarily incurred by the employee beyond $250 without our prior agreement, except for emergency measures reasonably necessary to protect the property from further loss.
4.2. Other insurance. If a loss covered by this contract is also covered by other insurance, we will pay only the proportion of the loss that the limit of liability that applies under this contract bears to the total amount of insurance covering the loss.
4.3. Recovered property. If the employee or we recover any property for which we have made payment, the employee must notify us. The property may be returned to the employee, in which case the loss payment is adjusted accordingly.

4.6. Subrogation. Any party covered under this contract may be required to assign to us rights of recovery against another party, up to the amount we have paid. The covered party must do nothing after loss to impair those rights.
4.7. Territorial limits. Coverage applies to losses occurring within the territory shown in the declarations. Property temporarily removed from the premises is covered for up to 5% of the applicable limit, but not for more than 45 consecutive days.
4.8. Assignment. Assignment of this contract is not valid unless we give our written consent.
4.9. Duties after loss. The employee must give notice as soon as practicable, protect the property from further damage, keep an accurate record of repair expenses, and produce receipts, inventories and other records that we reasonably request. A sworn proof of loss must be signed and delivered within 30 days after our request. These duties are conditions precedent to payment.

3. 'Repeated seepage or leakage' means water or steam escaping continuously or repeatedly for 10 days or longer.

5. 'Sudden and accidental discharge' means an escape of water that begins abruptly and is not repeated seepage or leakage.
6. 'Residence premises' means the one- or two-family dwelling where the insured resides, shown in the declarations, including structures attached to it.

======================================================================
PART C — COVERAGES
======================================================================
2.1. Emergency mitigation. Where water has escaped, the insured must arrange drying and dehumidification within 72 hours of discovery; the cost is covered as part of the loss up to $2,000.
2.2. Glass replacement. Loss for damage to glass caused by a covered peril includes the cost of replacing with safety glazing material when required by ordinance or law.
2.3. Reasonable repairs. We will pay the reasonable cost incurred by the insured for necessary measures taken solely to protect covered property from further damage after a covered loss, up to $1,000 without prior approval. This does not increase the limit of liability.
2.4. Loss settlement. Losses are settled at the cost to repair or replace with materials of like kind and quality, without deduction for depreciation, provided repair or replacement is completed within 180 days of the loss; otherwise on an actual cash value basis until completion.

======================================================================
PART D — GENERAL CONDITIONS
======================================================================
3.1. Intentional loss. We do not cover loss caused by an act that the insured committed, or directed someone else to commit, intending the loss to happen.
3.2. Duties after loss. The insured must give notice as soon as practicable, protect the property from further damage, keep an accurate record of repair expenses, and produce receipts, inventories and other records that we reasonably request. A sworn proof of loss must be signed and delivered within 30 days after our request. These duties are conditions precedent to payment.
3.3. Appraisal. If the parties fail to agree on the amount of loss, either may demand an appraisal. Each party selects a competent appraiser within 10 days; the appraisers select an umpire. question.instructions: How many exclusions bar cover for the building water damage in claim CLM-3923129, after applying any exceptions?

rationale: (1) The dwelling was without furnishings and empty for 7 days (not more than 90), so it was neither vacant nor unoccupied under the definitions. (2) The vacancy exclusion does not apply. (5) Decision: deny as repeated seepage with no exception. (6) Exclusions barring cover with no exception: 1.

SECTION 1 — PURPOSE AND SCOPE
======================================================================
This policy sets out when Umbra Industries reimburses relocation costs for employees who move at the company's request. It applies to all grades and locations.

======================================================================
SECTION 2 — RULES
======================================================================
1. Eligibility (distance test). A relocation is eligible only if the one-way distance from the employee's former home to the new workplace exceeds the distance from the former home to the former workplace by at least 40 km.
2. Time limit. Claims must be submitted with receipts within 120 days of the employee's start date at the new workplace. Where the employee is on approved leave during that period, the limit is extended by the number of leave days.
3. Caps. Reimbursement is capped by grade: G1 $4,000; G2 $6,000; G3 $10,000. Amounts above the cap are not reimbursed.
4. Dependants supplement. Where a spouse, partner or dependent child moves with the employee, the cap is increased by $2,000.
5. Excluded costs. Costs of buying or selling a home, mortgage penalties, and temporary accommodation beyond 30 nights are not reimbursable under this policy.
6. Repayment. An employee who leaves the company within 12 months of the start date must repay the reimbursement pro rata.

======================================================================
SECTION 3 — PROCESS
======================================================================
3.1. Advances. An advance of up to 50% of the applicable cap may be requested before the move; it is deducted from the final reimbursement. Unused advances must be repaid within 20 days.
3.2. Receipts. Only itemised receipts in the employee's name are accepted. Credit-card statements alone are not sufficient. Receipts in a foreign currency are converted at the company's monthly rate for the month of the expense.
3.3. Temporary accommodation. Where temporary accommodation is reimbursed, the employee must move to permanent accommodation within 30 nights; extensions require the approval of the HR director.
3.4. Definitions. 'Start date' means the first day the employee is required to attend the new workplace, as stated in the transfer letter. 'Former home' means the address on file on the date of the transfer letter.
3.5. Approvals. A relocation must be approved in writing by the receiving manager and by HR (Ulla Reinholt's team) before the move date. Approval is recorded on form RL-41 and attached to the employee's file.
3.6. Tax treatment. Reimbursements are reported in accordance with local tax rules. Where a reimbursement is taxable, the amount paid to the employee is not grossed up unless the offer letter says otherwise.
3.7. Interaction with other policies. Travel on the move day is reimbursed under this policy, not under the travel policy. Costs reimbursed under this policy are not claimable again under any other policy.
3.8. Data protection. Documents submitted with a claim are kept for 3 years after the claim is closed and are accessible only to HR and to the auditors.
3.9. Appeals. An employee may appeal a decision under this policy within 10 business days by writing to the HR director. The appeal is decided within 20 days; the decision on appeal is final.
3.10. Audit. Internal audit samples 5% of relocation claims each year. A claim found to be inaccurate may be recovered from salary in accordance with the deductions policy.

======================================================================
SECTION 4 — GENERAL PROVISIONS
======================================================================
4.1. Other insurance. If a loss covered by this contract is also covered by other insurance, we will pay only the proportion of the loss that the limit of liability that applies under this contract bears to the total amount of insurance covering the loss.
4.2. Volunteer payments. We will not pay for any expense voluntarily incurred by the employee beyond $1,000 without our prior agreement, except for emergency measures reasonably necessary to protect the property from further loss.

4.5. Concealment or fraud. We do not provide coverage if, whether before or after a loss, the employee has intentionally concealed or misrepresented any material fact or circumstance, engaged in fraudulent conduct, or made false statements relating to this contract.
4.6. Cancellation. The employee may cancel at any time by returning the contract to us or by notifying us in writing of the date cancellation is to take effect. We may cancel by mailing notice at least 30 days before the effective date, or 30 days where the cancellation is for reasons other than non-payment. Unearned premium is refunded pro rata.
4.7. Assignment. Assignment of this contract is not valid unless we give our written consent.
4.8. Neglect. We do not cover loss that results from the employee failing to take reasonable steps to protect and preserve the property once a loss has occurred.
4.9. Nuclear hazard. We do not cover loss caused directly or indirectly by nuclear reaction, radiation or radioactive contamination, whether controlled or uncontrolled, and whether or not caused by a peril otherwise covered.

======================================================================

======================================================================
AMENDMENT A-44 (effective 27 July 2025): for relocations where the employee's start date at the new workplace is on or after the effective date, the caps in rule 3 are increased to G1 $5,500; G2 $7,500; G3 $11,500. Relocations with earlier start dates remain on the previous caps.

1.3. Customer-caused outages. Minutes of unavailability caused by the customer's own equipment, credentials or configuration are not counted as downtime but remain in the denominator.
1.4. Scheduled maintenance outside the window. Maintenance performed outside the published window counts as downtime in full.
1.5. Service credit schedule (original): monthly uptime at or above 99.9%: no credit; at or above 99.5% but below 99.9%: 5% of the monthly fee; at or above 99.0% but below 99.5%: 10%; below 99.0%: 25%.
1.6. Claims. Credits must be claimed in writing within 30 days after the end of the month and are applied to the next invoice.

======================================================================
SECTION 2 — OPERATING PROCEDURES
======================================================================
2.1. Force majeure. Neither party is liable for delay or failure caused by events beyond its reasonable control, including natural disasters, war, and failures of public networks, provided the affected party notifies the other promptly.
2.2. Maintenance notices. Scheduled maintenance is announced at least 72 hours in advance through the status page. Maintenance that starts inside the window but runs beyond it counts as downtime for the minutes outside the window.
2.3. Credit application. Credits are applied to the invoice for the month after the report and are not paid in cash. Credits do not accumulate beyond the monthly fee.
2.4. Data handling. The provider processes customer data only as instructed and in accordance with the data processing schedule. Backups are retained for 60 days.
2.5. Incident classification. Each incident is classified by the provider within 5 business days after it closes; the customer may dispute a classification within 20 days by giving written reasons. Disputed classifications are reviewed by the service manager (Ulla Reinholt).
2.6. Monitoring. Availability is measured by the provider's monitoring system from three regions at one-minute intervals. A minute is unavailable if the service fails the health check from at least two regions.
2.7. Definitions. 'Available minutes' means minutes in the month in which the service passed the health check. 'Published maintenance window' means the window shown in the service description at the start of the month.

3.8. Interaction with other policies. Travel on the move day is reimbursed under this policy, not under the travel policy. Costs reimbursed under this policy are not claimable again under any other policy.
3.9. Appeals. An employee may appeal a decision under this policy within 5 business days by writing to the HR director. The appeal is decided within 45 days; the decision on appeal is final.

3. Caps. Reimbursement is capped by grade: G1 $4,000; G2 $7,500; G3 $10,000. Amounts above the cap are not reimbursed.

5. Excluded costs. Costs of buying or selling a home, mortgage penalties, and temporary accommodation beyond 30 nights are not reimbursable under this policy.

3.8. Definitions. 'Start date' means the first day the employee is required to attend the new workplace, as stated in the transfer letter. 'Former home' means the address on file on the date of the transfer letter.

======================================================================
SECTION 1 — PURPOSE AND SCOPE
======================================================================
This policy sets out when Tidewater Energy reimburses relocation costs for employees who move at the company's request. It applies to all grades and locations.

======================================================================
SECTION 2 — RULES
======================================================================
1. Eligibility (distance test). A relocation is eligible only if the one-way distance from the employee's former home to the new workplace exceeds the distance from the former home to the former workplace by at least 50 km.
2. Time limit. Claims must be submitted with receipts within 90 days of the employee's start date at the new workplace. Where the employee is on approved leave during that period, the limit is extended by the number of leave days.
3. Caps. Reimbursement is capped by grade: G1 $4,000; G2 $6,000; G3 $10,000. Amounts above the cap are not reimbursed.
4. Dependants supplement. Where a spouse, partner or dependent child moves with the employee, the cap is increased by $1,000.
5. Excluded costs. Costs of buying or selling a home, mortgage penalties, and temporary accommodation beyond 30 nights are not reimbursable under this policy.
6. Repayment. An employee who leaves the company within 12 months of the start date must repay the reimbursement pro rata.

======================================================================
SECTION 3 — PROCESS
======================================================================
3.1. Interaction with other policies. Travel on the move day is reimbursed under this policy, not under the travel policy. Costs reimbursed under this policy are not claimable again under any other policy.
3.2. Definitions. 'Start date' means the first day the employee is required to attend the new workplace, as stated in the transfer letter. 'Former home' means the address on file on the date of the transfer letter.
3.3. Advances. An advance of up to 50% of the applicable cap may be requested before the move; it is deducted from the final reimbursement. Unused advances must be repaid within 45 days.
3.4. Temporary accommodation. Where temporary accommodation is reimbursed, the employee must move to permanent accommodation within 30 nights; extensions require the approval of the HR director.
3.5. Receipts. Only itemised receipts in the employee's name are accepted. Credit-card statements alone are not sufficient. Receipts in a foreign currency are converted at the company's monthly rate for the month of the expense.
3.6. Appeals. An employee may appeal a decision under this policy within 10 business days by writing to the HR director. The appeal is decided within 45 days; the decision on appeal is final.
3.7. Data protection. Documents submitted with a claim are kept for 3 years after the claim is closed and are accessible only to HR and to the auditors.
3.8. Tax treatment. Reimbursements are reported in accordance with local tax rules. Where a reimbursement is taxable, the amount paid to the employee is not grossed up unless the offer letter says otherwise.
3.9. Audit. Internal audit samples 5% of relocation claims each year. A claim found to be inaccurate may be recovered from salary in accordance with the deductions policy.

======================================================================
SECTION 4 — GENERAL PROVISIONS
======================================================================
4.1. Other insurance. If a loss covered by this contract is also covered by other insurance, we will pay only the proportion of the loss that the limit of liability that applies under this contract bears to the total amount of insurance covering the loss.
4.2. Inflation guard. The limits shown in the declarations increase by 3% at each anniversary of the inception date unless this endorsement is deleted by the employee.
4.3. Salvage. When we pay for a loss we may take all or part of the damaged property at an agreed or appraised value. There is no abandonment of property to us.
4.4. Subrogation. Any party covered under this contract may be required to assign to us rights of recovery against another party, up to the amount we have paid. The covered party must do nothing after loss to impair those rights.
4.5. Volunteer payments. We will not pay for any expense voluntarily incurred by the employee beyond $1,000 without our prior agreement, except for emergency measures reasonably necessary to protect the property from further loss.
4.6. Neglect. We do not cover loss that results from the employee failing to take reasonable steps to protect and preserve the property once a loss has occurred.
4.7. Duties after loss. The employee must give notice as soon as practicable, protect the property from further damage, keep an accurate record of repair expenses, and produce receipts, inventories and other records that we reasonably request. A sworn proof of loss must be signed and delivered within 30 days after our request. These duties are conditions precedent to payment.
4.8. Suit against us. No action can be brought against us unless there has been full compliance with all of the terms of this contract and the action is started within 2 years after the date of loss.

======================================================================

This policy sets out when Ardent Systems reimburses relocation costs for employees who move at the company's request. It applies to all grades and locations.

======================================================================

======================================================================

2. Time limit. Claims must be submitted with receipts within 60 days of the employee's start date at the new workplace. Where the employee is on approved leave during that period, the limit is extended by the number of leave days.
3. Caps. Reimbursement is capped by grade: G1 $4,000; G2 $7,500; G3 $10,000. Amounts above the cap are not reimbursed.
4. Dependants supplement. Where a spouse, partner or dependent child moves with the employee, the cap is increased by $1,500.
5. Excluded costs. Costs of buying or selling a home, mortgage penalties, and temporary accommodation beyond 30 nights are not reimbursable under this policy.
6. Repayment. An employee who leaves the company within 12 months of the start date must repay the reimbursement pro rata.

======================================================================

======================================================================
3.1. Interaction with other policies. Travel on the move day is reimbursed under this policy, not under the travel policy. Costs reimbursed under this policy are not claimable again under any other policy.

======================================================================
SECTION 1 — PURPOSE AND SCOPE
======================================================================
This policy sets out when Halcyon Systems reimburses relocation costs for employees who move at the company's request. It applies to all grades and locations.

======================================================================
SECTION 2 — RULES
======================================================================
1. Eligibility (distance test). A relocation is eligible only if the one-way distance from the employee's former home to the new workplace exceeds the distance from the former home to the former workplace by at least 50 km.
2. Time limit. Claims must be submitted with receipts within 90 days of the employee's start date at the new workplace. Where the employee is on approved leave during that period, the limit is extended by the number of leave days.
3. Caps. Reimbursement is capped by grade: G1 $4,000; G2 $7,500; G3 $12,000. Amounts above the cap are not reimbursed.
4. Dependants supplement. Where a spouse, partner or dependent child moves with the employee, the cap is increased by $2,000.
5. Excluded costs. Costs of buying or selling a home, mortgage penalties, and temporary accommodation beyond 30 nights are not reimbursable under this policy.
6. Repayment. An employee who leaves the company within 12 months of the start date must repay the reimbursement pro rata.

======================================================================
SECTION 3 — PROCESS
======================================================================
3.1. Advances. An advance of up to 50% of the applicable cap may be requested before the move; it is deducted from the final reimbursement. Unused advances must be repaid within 20 days.
3.2. Data protection. Documents submitted with a claim are kept for 7 years after the claim is closed and are accessible only to HR and to the auditors.
3.3. Appeals. An employee may appeal a decision under this policy within 5 business days by writing to the HR director. The appeal is decided within 20 days; the decision on appeal is final.
3.4. Approvals. A relocation must be approved in writing by the receiving manager and by HR (Tomasz Sandoval's team) before the move date. Approval is recorded on form RL-51 and attached to the employee's file.
3.5. Temporary accommodation. Where temporary accommodation is reimbursed, the employee must move to permanent accommodation within 30 nights; extensions require the approval of the HR director.
3.6. Definitions. 'Start date' means the first day the employee is required to attend the new workplace, as stated in the transfer letter. 'Former home' means the address on file on the date of the transfer letter.
3.7. Audit. Internal audit samples 10% of relocation claims each year. A claim found to be inaccurate may be recovered from salary in accordance with the deductions policy.
3.8. Receipts. Only itemised receipts in the employee's name are accepted. Credit-card statements alone are not sufficient. Receipts in a foreign currency are converted at the company's monthly rate for the month of the expense.
3.9. Tax treatment. Reimbursements are reported in accordance with local tax rules. Where a reimbursement is taxable, the amount paid to the employee is not grossed up unless the offer letter says otherwise.

======================================================================
SECTION 4 — GENERAL PROVISIONS
======================================================================
4.1. Ordinance or law. Extra cost caused by having to comply with building codes or other regulations when repairing, rebuilding or demolishing is covered up to 5% of the Coverage A limit.
4.2. Loss payment. We will adjust all losses with the employee and pay within 30 days after we reach agreement, after entry of a final judgment, or after the filing of an appraisal award with us, whichever comes first.

4.4. Assignment. Assignment of this contract is not valid unless we give our written consent.
4.5. Appraisal. If the parties fail to agree on the amount of loss, either may demand an appraisal. Each party selects a competent appraiser within 30 days; the appraisers select an umpire. A decision agreed to by any two is binding. Each party pays its own appraiser and shares the cost of the umpire equally.
4.6. Nuclear hazard. We do not cover loss caused directly or indirectly by nuclear reaction, radiation or radioactive contamination, whether controlled or uncontrolled, and whether or not caused by a peril otherwise covered.

Denial of the employee's claim does not apply to a valid claim of the mortgagee if the mortgagee notifies us of any change in ownership, occupancy or substantial change in risk of which it is aware.
4.8. Salvage. When we pay for a loss we may take all or part of the damaged property at an agreed or appraised value. There is no abandonment of property to us.
4.9. Territorial limits. Coverage applies to losses occurring within the territory shown in the declarations. Property temporarily removed from the premises is covered for up to 5% of the applicable limit, but not for more than 45 consecutive days.
4.10. Concealment or fraud. We do not provide coverage if, whether before or after a loss, the employee has intentionally concealed or misrepresented any material fact or circumstance, engaged in fraudulent conduct, or made false statements relating to this contract.

question.instructions: Is any part of the building water damage in claim CLM-7568550 payable under the policy?

rationale: (1) The dwelling was furnished and empty for 60 days (more than 30), so it was unoccupied under the definitions. (2) The vacancy exclusion does not apply. criteria.deny_vacant_dwelling: Deny: the vacancy exclusion (4.7) bars the building water damage and no exception restores cover.

criteria.pay_within_5000_sublimit: Pay: cover is restored by the concealed-water exception, capped at $5,000 after the deductible.
criteria.pay_within_15000_sublimit: Pay: cover is restored by the concealed-water exception, capped at $15,000 after the deductible.
criteria.pay_estimate_less_deductible: Pay in full: no exclusion or sublimit applies; the repair estimate minus the deductible is payable.

rationale: (1) The dwelling was without furnishings and empty for 60 days (more than 45), so it was vacant under the definitions. (2) The vacancy exclusion applies. (3) 21 days is at least 21 days, so the water is 'repeated seepage or leakage'. 1. Eligibility (distance test). A relocation is eligible only if the one-way distance from the employee's former home to the new workplace exceeds the distance from the former home to the former workplace by at least 40 km.

3. Caps. Reimbursement is capped by grade: G1 $4,000; G2 $7,500; G3 $10,000. Amounts above the cap are not reimbursed.
4. Dependants supplement. Where a spouse, partner or dependent child moves with the employee, the cap is increased by $1,500.
5. Excluded costs. Costs of buying or selling a home, mortgage penalties, and temporary accommodation beyond 30 nights are not reimbursable under this policy.
6. Repayment. An employee who leaves the company within 12 months of the start date must repay the reimbursement pro rata.

======================================================================
SECTION 3 — PROCESS
======================================================================
3.1. Receipts. Only itemised receipts in the employee's name are accepted. Credit-card statements alone are not sufficient. Receipts in a foreign currency are converted at the company's monthly rate for the month of the expense.
3.2. Data protection. Documents submitted with a claim are kept for 7 years after the claim is closed and are accessible only to HR and to the auditors.
3.3. Interaction with other policies. Travel on the move day is reimbursed under this policy, not under the travel policy. Costs reimbursed under this policy are not claimable again under any other policy.
3.4. Appeals. An employee may appeal a decision under this policy within 15 business days by writing to the HR director. The appeal is decided within 20 days; the decision on appeal is final.
3.5. Approvals. A relocation must be approved in writing by the receiving manager and by HR (Wendel Jansen's team) before the move date. Approval is recorded on form RL-28 and attached to the employee's file.
3.6. Temporary accommodation. Where temporary accommodation is reimbursed, the employee must move to permanent accommodation within 30 nights; extensions require the approval of the HR director.

======================================================================

4.3. Neglect. We do not cover loss that results from the employee failing to take reasonable steps to protect and preserve the property once a loss has occurred.

SECTION 1 — PURPOSE AND SCOPE
======================================================================
This policy sets out when Kestrel Technologies reimburses relocation costs for employees who move at the company's request. It applies to all grades and locations.

======================================================================
SECTION 2 — RULES
======================================================================
1. Eligibility (distance test). A relocation is eligible only if the one-way distance from the employee's former home to the new workplace exceeds the distance from the former home to the former workplace by at least 50 km.
2. Time limit. Claims must be submitted with receipts within 120 days of the employee's start date at the new workplace. Where the employee is on approved leave during that period, the limit is extended by the number of leave days.
3. Caps. Reimbursement is capped by grade: G1 $4,000; G2 $7,500; G3 $10,000. Amounts above the cap are not reimbursed.
4. Dependants supplement. Where a spouse, partner or dependent child moves with the employee, the cap is increased by $1,000.
5. Excluded costs. Costs of buying or selling a home, mortgage penalties, and temporary accommodation beyond 30 nights are not reimbursable under this policy.
6. Repayment. An employee who leaves the company within 12 months of the start date must repay the reimbursement pro rata.

======================================================================
SECTION 3 — PROCESS
======================================================================
3.1. Interaction with other policies. Travel on the move day is reimbursed under this policy, not under the travel policy. Costs reimbursed under this policy are not claimable again under any other policy.
3.2. Audit. Internal audit samples 10% of relocation claims each year. A claim found to be inaccurate may be recovered from salary in accordance with the deductions policy.
3.3. Definitions. 'Start date' means the first day the employee is required to attend the new workplace, as stated in the transfer letter. 'Former home' means the address on file on the date of the transfer letter.
3.4. Receipts. Only itemised receipts in the employee's name are accepted. Credit-card statements alone are not sufficient. Receipts in a foreign currency are converted at the company's monthly rate for the month of the expense.
3.5. Advances. An advance of up to 50% of the applicable cap may be requested before the move; it is deducted from the final reimbursement. Unused advances must be repaid within 30 days.
3.6. Temporary accommodation. Where temporary accommodation is reimbursed, the employee must move to permanent accommodation within 30 nights; extensions require the approval of the HR director.
3.7. Tax treatment. Reimbursements are reported in accordance with local tax rules. Where a reimbursement is taxable, the amount paid to the employee is not grossed up unless the offer letter says otherwise.

======================================================================
SECTION 4 — GENERAL PROVISIONS
======================================================================
4.1. Appraisal. If the parties fail to agree on the amount of loss, either may demand an appraisal. Each party selects a competent appraiser within 21 days; the appraisers select an umpire. A decision agreed to by any two is binding. Each party pays its own appraiser and shares the cost of the umpire equally.
4.2. Inflation guard. The limits shown in the declarations increase by 4% at each anniversary of the inception date unless this endorsement is deleted by the employee.
4.3. Assignment. Assignment of this contract is not valid unless we give our written consent.

4.5. Waiver or change of provisions. A waiver or change of a provision of this contract must be in writing by us to be valid. Our request for an appraisal or examination does not waive any of our rights.
4.6. Salvage. When we pay for a loss we may take all or part of the damaged property at an agreed or appraised value. There is no abandonment of property to us.
4.7. Duties after loss. The employee must give notice as soon as practicable, protect the property from further damage, keep an accurate record of repair expenses, and produce receipts, inventories and other records that we reasonably request. A sworn proof of loss must be signed and delivered within 30 days after our request. These duties are conditions precedent to payment.
4.8. Volunteer payments. We will not pay for any expense voluntarily incurred by the employee beyond $1,000 without our prior agreement, except for emergency measures reasonably necessary to protect the property from further loss.
4.9. Subrogation. Any party covered under this contract may be required to assign to us rights of recovery against another party, up to the amount we have paid. The covered party must do nothing after loss to impair those rights.

question.instructions: How should claim CLM-3819505 for the building water damage be decided under the policy as it stands?

criteria.deny_vacant_dwelling: Deny: the vacancy exclusion (4.7) bars the building water damage and no exception restores cover.
criteria.deny_repeated_leakage: Deny: the repeated-seepage exclusion (4.3) bars the loss and the concealed-water exception does not restore it.
criteria.pay_within_7500_sublimit: Pay: cover is restored by the concealed-water exception, capped at $7,500 after the deductible.
criteria.pay_within_17500_sublimit: Pay: cover is restored by the concealed-water exception, capped at $17,500 after the deductible.
criteria.pay_estimate_less_deductible: Pay in full: no exclusion or sublimit applies; the repair estimate minus the deductible is payable.

rationale: (1) The dwelling was furnished and empty for 29 days (not more than 30), so it was neither vacant nor unoccupied under the definitions. (2) The vacancy exclusion does not apply. (3) 11 days is less than 14 days, so the water is not 'repeated seepage or leakage'. (4) Decision: sudden discharge, covered in full less the deductible: $4,500.

3.7. Tax treatment. Reimbursements are reported in accordance with local tax rules. Where a reimbursement is taxable, the amount paid to the employee is not grossed up unless the offer letter says otherwise.
3.8. Interaction with other policies. Travel on the move day is reimbursed under this policy, not under the travel policy. Costs reimbursed under this policy are not claimable again under any other policy.
3.9. Definitions. 'Start date' means the first day the employee is required to attend the new workplace, as stated in the transfer letter. 'Former home' means the address on file on the date of the transfer letter.
3.10. Advances. An advance of up to 50% of the applicable cap may be requested before the move; it is deducted from the final reimbursement. Unused advances must be repaid within 30 days.

4.6. Definitions of general application. In this contract 'we' and 'us' mean the insurer that issued it, and 'you' means the employee shown on the declarations page. 'Business day' means a day other than Saturday, Sunday or a public holiday at the place shown in the declarations.
4.7. Assignment. Assignment of this contract is not valid unless we give our written consent.
4.8. Territorial limits. Coverage applies to losses occurring within the territory shown in the declarations. Property temporarily removed from the premises is covered for up to 15% of the applicable limit, but not for more than 30 consecutive days.
4.9. Appraisal. If the parties fail to agree on the amount of loss, either may demand an appraisal. Each party selects a competent appraiser within 30 days; the appraisers select an umpire. A decision agreed to by any two is binding. Each party pays its own appraiser and shares the cost of the umpire equally.

3. Caps. Reimbursement is capped by grade: G1 $3,000; G2 $7,500; G3 $12,000. Amounts above the cap are not reimbursed.
4. Dependants supplement. Where a spouse, partner or dependent child moves with the employee, the cap is increased by $2,000.
5. Excluded costs. Costs of buying or selling a home, mortgage penalties, and temporary accommodation beyond 30 nights are not reimbursable under this policy.
6. Repayment. An employee who leaves the company within 12 months of the start date must repay the reimbursement pro rata.

======================================================================
3.1. Approvals. A relocation must be approved in writing by the receiving manager and by HR (Bram Jansen's team) before the move date. Approval is recorded on form RL-48 and attached to the employee's file.
3.2. Definitions. 'Start date' means the first day the employee is required to attend the new workplace, as stated in the transfer letter. 'Former home' means the address on file on the date of the transfer letter.
3.3. Appeals. An employee may appeal a decision under this policy within 15 business days by writing to the HR director. The appeal is decided within 20 days; the decision on appeal is final.
3.4. Tax treatment. Reimbursements are reported in accordance with local tax rules. Where a reimbursement is taxable, the amount paid to the employee is not grossed up unless the offer letter says otherwise.
3.5. Audit. Internal audit samples 10% of relocation claims each year. A claim found to be inaccurate may be recovered from salary in accordance with the deductions policy.
3.6. Data protection. Documents submitted with a claim are kept for 3 years after the claim is closed and are accessible only to HR and to the auditors.
3.7. Advances. An advance of up to 50% of the applicable cap may be requested before the move; it is deducted from the final reimbursement. Unused advances must be repaid within 20 days.
