SECTION 1 — PURPOSE AND SCOPE
======================================================================
This policy sets out when Ashcombe Technologies reimburses relocation costs for employees who move at the company's request. It applies to all grades and locations.

======================================================================
SECTION 2 — RULES
======================================================================
1. Eligibility (distance test). A relocation is eligible only if the one-way distance from the employee's former home to the new workplace exceeds the distance from the former home to the former workplace by at least 80 km.
2. Time limit. Claims must be submitted with receipts within 90 days of the employee's start date at the new workplace. Where the employee is on approved leave during that period, the limit is extended by the number of leave days.
3. Caps. Reimbursement is capped by grade: G1 $3,000; G2 $7,500; G3 $10,000. Amounts above the cap are not reimbursed.
4. Dependants supplement. Where a spouse, partner or dependent child moves with the employee, the cap is increased by $1,000.
5. Excluded costs. Costs of buying or selling a home, mortgage penalties, and temporary accommodation beyond 30 nights are not reimbursable under this policy.
6. Repayment. An employee who leaves the company within 12 months of the start date must repay the reimbursement pro rata.

======================================================================
SECTION 3 — PROCESS
======================================================================
3.1. Receipts. Only itemised receipts in the employee's name are accepted. Credit-card statements alone are not sufficient. Receipts in a foreign currency are converted at the company's monthly rate for the month of the expense.
3.2. Approvals. A relocation must be approved in writing by the receiving manager and by HR (Cerys Tanaka's team) before the move date. Approval is recorded on form RL-10 and attached to the employee's file.
3.3. Audit. Internal audit samples 10% of relocation claims each year. A claim found to be inaccurate may be recovered from salary in accordance with the deductions policy.
3.4. Appeals. An employee may appeal a decision under this policy within 5 business days by writing to the HR director. The appeal is decided within 20 days; the decision on appeal is final.
3.5. Tax treatment. Reimbursements are reported in accordance with local tax rules. Where a reimbursement is taxable, the amount paid to the employee is not grossed up unless the offer letter says otherwise.
3.6. Advances. An advance of up to 50% of the applicable cap may be requested before the move; it is deducted from the final reimbursement. Unused advances must be repaid within 20 days.
3.7. Definitions. 'Start date' means the first day the employee is required to attend the new workplace, as stated in the transfer letter. 'Former home' means the address on file on the date of the transfer letter.
3.8. Interaction with other policies. Travel on the move day is reimbursed under this policy, not under the travel policy. Costs reimbursed under this policy are not claimable again under any other policy.
3.9. Data protection. Documents submitted with a claim are kept for 3 years after the claim is closed and are accessible only to HR and to the auditors.
3.10. Temporary accommodation. Where temporary accommodation is reimbursed, the employee must move to permanent accommodation within 30 nights; extensions require the approval of the HR director.

======================================================================
SECTION 4 — GENERAL PROVISIONS
======================================================================
4.1. War. We do not cover loss caused by war, including undeclared war, civil war, insurrection, rebellion or revolution, or by warlike acts of a military force or personnel.

criteria.deny_vacant_dwelling: Deny: the vacancy exclusion (4.7) bars the building water damage and no exception restores cover.

criteria.pay_within_7500_sublimit: Pay: cover is restored by the concealed-water exception, capped at $7,500 after the deductible.
criteria.pay_within_12500_sublimit: Pay: cover is restored by the concealed-water exception, capped at $12,500 after the deductible.
criteria.pay_estimate_less_deductible: Pay in full: no exclusion or sublimit applies; the repair estimate minus the deductible is payable.

rationale: (1) The dwelling was without furnishings and empty for 12 days (not more than 60), so it was neither vacant nor unoccupied under the definitions. (2) The vacancy exclusion does not apply. (3) 14 days is at least 14 days, so the water is 'repeated seepage or leakage'. (4) The concealed-water exception applies: the water was hidden and unknown to the insured, so cover is restored subject to the sublimit. (5) The term was renewed on or after 26 December 2025, so the concealed-water sublimit is $12,500. (6) Decision: pay, subject to the $12,500 sublimit ($6,000 - $1,000 = $5,000, capped at $12,500 = $5,000).

This policy sets out when Halcyon Industries reimburses relocation costs for employees who move at the company's request. It applies to all grades and locations.

======================================================================
1. Eligibility (distance test). A relocation is eligible only if the one-way distance from the employee's former home to the new workplace exceeds the distance from the former home to the former workplace by at least 40 km.
2. Time limit. Claims must be submitted with receipts within 120 days of the employee's start date at the new workplace. Where the employee is on approved leave during that period, the limit is extended by the number of leave days.
3. Caps. Reimbursement is capped by grade: G1 $3,000; G2 $7,500; G3 $10,000. Amounts above the cap are not reimbursed.
4. Dependants supplement. Where a spouse, partner or dependent child moves with the employee, the cap is increased by $2,000.
5. Excluded costs. Costs of buying or selling a home, mortgage penalties, and temporary accommodation beyond 30 nights are not reimbursable under this policy.
6. Repayment. An employee who leaves the company within 12 months of the start date must repay the reimbursement pro rata.

======================================================================
SECTION 3 — PROCESS
======================================================================
3.1. Audit. Internal audit samples 5% of relocation claims each year. A claim found to be inaccurate may be recovered from salary in accordance with the deductions policy.
3.2. Definitions. 'Start date' means the first day the employee is required to attend the new workplace, as stated in the transfer letter. 'Former home' means the address on file on the date of the transfer letter.
3.3. Advances. An advance of up to 50% of the applicable cap may be requested before the move; it is deducted from the final reimbursement. Unused advances must be repaid within 30 days.
3.4. Receipts. Only itemised receipts in the employee's name are accepted. Credit-card statements alone are not sufficient. Receipts in a foreign currency are converted at the company's monthly rate for the month of the expense.
3.5. Appeals. An employee may appeal a decision under this policy within 5 business days by writing to the HR director. The appeal is decided within 30 days; the decision on appeal is final.
3.6. Approvals. A relocation must be approved in writing by the receiving manager and by HR (Aiko Villanueva's team) before the move date. Approval is recorded on form RL-72 and attached to the employee's file.
3.7. Interaction with other policies. Travel on the move day is reimbursed under this policy, not under the travel policy. Costs reimbursed under this policy are not claimable again under any other policy.
3.8. Tax treatment. Reimbursements are reported in accordance with local tax rules. Where a reimbursement is taxable, the amount paid to the employee is not grossed up unless the offer letter says otherwise.

======================================================================

======================================================================
SECTION 1 — PURPOSE AND SCOPE
======================================================================
This policy sets out when Juniper Technologies reimburses relocation costs for employees who move at the company's request. It applies to all grades and locations.

======================================================================
SECTION 2 — RULES
======================================================================
1. Eligibility (distance test). A relocation is eligible only if the one-way distance from the employee's former home to the new workplace exceeds the distance from the former home to the former workplace by at least 40 km.
2. Time limit. Claims must be submitted with receipts within 120 days of the employee's start date at the new workplace. Where the employee is on approved leave during that period, the limit is extended by the number of leave days.
3. Caps. Reimbursement is capped by grade: G1 $3,000; G2 $7,500; G3 $12,000. Amounts above the cap are not reimbursed.
4. Dependants supplement. Where a spouse, partner or dependent child moves with the employee, the cap is increased by $2,000.
5. Excluded costs. Costs of buying or selling a home, mortgage penalties, and temporary accommodation beyond 30 nights are not reimbursable under this policy.
6. Repayment. An employee who leaves the company within 12 months of the start date must repay the reimbursement pro rata.

======================================================================
SECTION 3 — PROCESS
======================================================================
3.1. Advances. An advance of up to 50% of the applicable cap may be requested before the move; it is deducted from the final reimbursement. Unused advances must be repaid within 45 days.
3.2. Definitions. 'Start date' means the first day the employee is required to attend the new workplace, as stated in the transfer letter. 'Former home' means the address on file on the date of the transfer letter.
3.3. Appeals. An employee may appeal a decision under this policy within 15 business days by writing to the HR director. The appeal is decided within 45 days; the decision on appeal is final.
3.4. Data protection. Documents submitted with a claim are kept for 5 years after the claim is closed and are accessible only to HR and to the auditors.
3.5. Interaction with other policies. Travel on the move day is reimbursed under this policy, not under the travel policy. Costs reimbursed under this policy are not claimable again under any other policy.
3.6. Approvals. A relocation must be approved in writing by the receiving manager and by HR (Cerys Grieg's team) before the move date. Approval is recorded on form RL-21 and attached to the employee's file.
3.7. Receipts. Only itemised receipts in the employee's name are accepted. Credit-card statements alone are not sufficient. Receipts in a foreign currency are converted at the company's monthly rate for the month of the expense.

======================================================================
SECTION 4 — GENERAL PROVISIONS
======================================================================
4.1. Intentional loss. We do not cover loss caused by an act that the employee committed, or directed someone else to commit, intending the loss to happen.
4.2. Electronic data. Loss of or damage to electronic data is covered only for the cost of blank media and the cost of copying from backups, subject to a limit of $2,500 per occurrence.
4.3. Nuclear hazard. We do not cover loss caused directly or indirectly by nuclear reaction, radiation or radioactive contamination, whether controlled or uncontrolled, and whether or not caused by a peril otherwise covered.
4.4. Recovered property. If the employee or we recover any property for which we have made payment, the employee must notify us. The property may be returned to the employee, in which case the loss payment is adjusted accordingly.
4.5. Neglect. We do not cover loss that results from the employee failing to take reasonable steps to protect and preserve the property once a loss has occurred.
4.6. Suit against us. No action can be brought against us unless there has been full compliance with all of the terms of this contract and the action is started within 3 years after the date of loss.
4.7. Concealment or fraud. We do not provide coverage if, whether before or after a loss, the employee has intentionally concealed or misrepresented any material fact or circumstance, engaged in fraudulent conduct, or made false statements relating to this contract.
4.8. Assignment. Assignment of this contract is not valid unless we give our written consent.
4.9. Inflation guard. The limits shown in the declarations increase by 3% at each anniversary of the inception date unless this endorsement is deleted by the employee.
4.10. Salvage. When we pay for a loss we may take all or part of the damaged property at an agreed or appraised value. There is no abandonment of property to us.

======================================================================
SECTION 5 — AMENDMENTS
======================================================================
AMENDMENT A-85 (effective 29 July 2026): for relocations where the employee's start date at the new workplace is on or after the effective date, the caps in rule 3 are increased to G1 $5,500; G2 $10,000; G3 $14,500. Relocations with earlier start dates remain on the previous caps.

======================================================================
SECTION 6 — CASE FILE REL-897712
======================================================================
Case REL-897712. Employee: Ines Iversen (EMP-54447), grade G1. Former workplace: Sydney office. New workplace: Vienna plant. Start date at new workplace: 26 July 2026.
Distances (from the former home, one way, per the routing tool): to former workplace 12 km; to new workplace 52 km.
Household: the employee relocated alone.
Claim submitted 13 November 2026 with receipts totalling $7,800 (removal contractor, travel, utility connections).

question.instructions: How should claim CLM-7211443 for the building water damage be decided under the policy as it stands?

criteria.deny_vacant_dwelling: Deny: the vacancy exclusion (4.7) bars the building water damage and no exception restores cover.
criteria.deny_repeated_leakage: Deny: the repeated-seepage exclusion (4.3) bars the loss and the concealed-water exception does not restore it.
criteria.pay_within_10000_sublimit: Pay: cover is restored by the concealed-water exception, capped at $10,000 after the deductible.
criteria.pay_within_20000_sublimit: Pay: cover is restored by the concealed-water exception, capped at $20,000 after the deductible.
criteria.pay_estimate_less_deductible: Pay in full: no exclusion or sublimit applies; the repair estimate minus the deductible is payable.

rationale: (1) The dwelling was furnished and empty for 45 days (more than 30), so it was unoccupied under the definitions. (2) The vacancy exclusion does not apply. (3) 10 days is at least 10 days, so the water is 'repeated seepage or leakage'. (4) The concealed-water exception applies: the water was hidden and unknown to the insured, so cover is restored subject to the sublimit. (5) The term was renewed on or after 25 May 2025, so the concealed-water sublimit is $20,000. (6) Decision: pay, subject to the $20,000 sublimit ($12,400 - $1,000 = $11,400, capped at $20,000 = $11,400).

======================================================================
This policy sets out when Quarry Energy reimburses relocation costs for employees who move at the company's request. It applies to all grades and locations.

======================================================================

======================================================================
1. Eligibility (distance test). A relocation is eligible only if the one-way distance from the employee's former home to the new workplace exceeds the distance from the former home to the former workplace by at least 40 km.
2. Time limit. Claims must be submitted with receipts within 90 days of the employee's start date at the new workplace. Where the employee is on approved leave during that period, the limit is extended by the number of leave days.
3. Caps. Reimbursement is capped by grade: G1 $3,000; G2 $7,500; G3 $10,000. Amounts above the cap are not reimbursed.
4. Dependants supplement. Where a spouse, partner or dependent child moves with the employee, the cap is increased by $1,500.
5. Excluded costs. Costs of buying or selling a home, mortgage penalties, and temporary accommodation beyond 30 nights are not reimbursable under this policy.
6. Repayment. An employee who leaves the company within 12 months of the start date must repay the reimbursement pro rata.

======================================================================
SECTION 3 — PROCESS
======================================================================
3.1. Audit. Internal audit samples 5% of relocation claims each year. A claim found to be inaccurate may be recovered from salary in accordance with the deductions policy.
3.2. Definitions. 'Start date' means the first day the employee is required to attend the new workplace, as stated in the transfer letter. 'Former home' means the address on file on the date of the transfer letter.
3.3. Temporary accommodation. Where temporary accommodation is reimbursed, the employee must move to permanent accommodation within 30 nights; extensions require the approval of the HR director.
3.4. Appeals. An employee may appeal a decision under this policy within 5 business days by writing to the HR director. The appeal is decided within 20 days; the decision on appeal is final.
3.5. Data protection. Documents submitted with a claim are kept for 3 years after the claim is closed and are accessible only to HR and to the auditors.
3.6. Interaction with other policies. Travel on the move day is reimbursed under this policy, not under the travel policy. Costs reimbursed under this policy are not claimable again under any other policy.
3.7. Receipts. Only itemised receipts in the employee's name are accepted. Credit-card statements alone are not sufficient. Receipts in a foreign currency are converted at the company's monthly rate for the month of the expense.

======================================================================
SECTION 4 — GENERAL PROVISIONS
======================================================================
4.1. Electronic data. Loss of or damage to electronic data is covered only for the cost of blank media and the cost of copying from backups, subject to a limit of $2,500 per occurrence.

SECTION 1 — PURPOSE AND SCOPE
======================================================================
This policy sets out when Marlow Industries reimburses relocation costs for employees who move at the company's request. It applies to all grades and locations.

======================================================================

======================================================================
1. Eligibility (distance test). A relocation is eligible only if the one-way distance from the employee's former home to the new workplace exceeds the distance from the former home to the former workplace by at least 60 km.

3. Caps. Reimbursement is capped by grade: G1 $4,000; G2 $7,500; G3 $10,000. Amounts above the cap are not reimbursed.
4. Dependants supplement. Where a spouse, partner or dependent child moves with the employee, the cap is increased by $2,000.
5. Excluded costs. Costs of buying or selling a home, mortgage penalties, and temporary accommodation beyond 30 nights are not reimbursable under this policy.
6. Repayment. An employee who leaves the company within 12 months of the start date must repay the reimbursement pro rata.

======================================================================
SECTION 3 — PROCESS
======================================================================
3.1. Temporary accommodation. Where temporary accommodation is reimbursed, the employee must move to permanent accommodation within 30 nights; extensions require the approval of the HR director.
3.2. Definitions. 'Start date' means the first day the employee is required to attend the new workplace, as stated in the transfer letter. 'Former home' means the address on file on the date of the transfer letter.
3.3. Tax treatment. Reimbursements are reported in accordance with local tax rules. Where a reimbursement is taxable, the amount paid to the employee is not grossed up unless the offer letter says otherwise.
3.4. Interaction with other policies. Travel on the move day is reimbursed under this policy, not under the travel policy. Costs reimbursed under this policy are not claimable again under any other policy.
3.5. Advances. An advance of up to 50% of the applicable cap may be requested before the move; it is deducted from the final reimbursement. Unused advances must be repaid within 20 days.
3.6. Data protection. Documents submitted with a claim are kept for 7 years after the claim is closed and are accessible only to HR and to the auditors.
3.7. Audit. Internal audit samples 5% of relocation claims each year. A claim found to be inaccurate may be recovered from salary in accordance with the deductions policy.
3.8. Approvals. A relocation must be approved in writing by the receiving manager and by HR (Ximena Fontaine's team) before the move date. Approval is recorded on form RL-40 and attached to the employee's file.
3.9. Receipts. Only itemised receipts in the employee's name are accepted. Credit-card statements alone are not sufficient. Receipts in a foreign currency are converted at the company's monthly rate for the month of the expense.

======================================================================
SECTION 4 — GENERAL PROVISIONS
======================================================================
4.1. Loss payment. We will adjust all losses with the employee and pay within 60 days after we reach agreement, after entry of a final judgment, or after the filing of an appraisal award with us, whichever comes first.
4.2. Volunteer payments. We will not pay for any expense voluntarily incurred by the employee beyond $1,000 without our prior agreement, except for emergency measures reasonably necessary to protect the property from further loss.

4.6. Suit against us. No action can be brought against us unless there has been full compliance with all of the terms of this contract and the action is started within 1 year after the date of loss.
4.7. Duties after loss. The employee must give notice as soon as practicable, protect the property from further damage, keep an accurate record of repair expenses, and produce receipts, inventories and other records that we reasonably request. A sworn proof of loss must be signed and delivered within 60 days after our request. These duties are conditions precedent to payment.
4.8. Recovered property. If the employee or we recover any property for which we have made payment, the employee must notify us. The property may be returned to the employee, in which case the loss payment is adjusted accordingly.
4.9. Subrogation. Any party covered under this contract may be required to assign to us rights of recovery against another party, up to the amount we have paid. The covered party must do nothing after loss to impair those rights.
4.10. Ordinance or law. Extra cost caused by having to comply with building codes or other regulations when repairing, rebuilding or demolishing is covered up to 15% of the Coverage A limit.

SECTION 1 — PURPOSE AND SCOPE
======================================================================
This policy sets out when Marlow Technologies reimburses relocation costs for employees who move at the company's request. It applies to all grades and locations.

======================================================================
SECTION 2 — RULES
======================================================================
1. Eligibility (distance test). A relocation is eligible only if the one-way distance from the employee's former home to the new workplace exceeds the distance from the former home to the former workplace by at least 50 km.
2. Time limit. Claims must be submitted with receipts within 120 days of the employee's start date at the new workplace. Where the employee is on approved leave during that period, the limit is extended by the number of leave days.
3. Caps. Reimbursement is capped by grade: G1 $4,000; G2 $6,000; G3 $10,000. Amounts above the cap are not reimbursed.
4. Dependants supplement. Where a spouse, partner or dependent child moves with the employee, the cap is increased by $1,500.
5. Excluded costs. Costs of buying or selling a home, mortgage penalties, and temporary accommodation beyond 30 nights are not reimbursable under this policy.
6. Repayment. An employee who leaves the company within 12 months of the start date must repay the reimbursement pro rata.

======================================================================
SECTION 3 — PROCESS
======================================================================
3.1. Advances. An advance of up to 50% of the applicable cap may be requested before the move; it is deducted from the final reimbursement. Unused advances must be repaid within 30 days.
3.2. Definitions. 'Start date' means the first day the employee is required to attend the new workplace, as stated in the transfer letter. 'Former home' means the address on file on the date of the transfer letter.
3.3. Tax treatment. Reimbursements are reported in accordance with local tax rules. Where a reimbursement is taxable, the amount paid to the employee is not grossed up unless the offer letter says otherwise.
3.4. Audit. Internal audit samples 10% of relocation claims each year. A claim found to be inaccurate may be recovered from salary in accordance with the deductions policy.
3.5. Interaction with other policies. Travel on the move day is reimbursed under this policy, not under the travel policy. Costs reimbursed under this policy are not claimable again under any other policy.
3.6. Approvals. A relocation must be approved in writing by the receiving manager and by HR (Halima Zanetti's team) before the move date. Approval is recorded on form RL-14 and attached to the employee's file.
3.7. Temporary accommodation. Where temporary accommodation is reimbursed, the employee must move to permanent accommodation within 30 nights; extensions require the approval of the HR director.
3.8. Receipts. Only itemised receipts in the employee's name are accepted. Credit-card statements alone are not sufficient. Receipts in a foreign currency are converted at the company's monthly rate for the month of the expense.
3.9. Appeals. An employee may appeal a decision under this policy within 10 business days by writing to the HR director. The appeal is decided within 30 days; the decision on appeal is final.

======================================================================
SECTION 4 — GENERAL PROVISIONS
======================================================================
4.1. Subrogation. Any party covered under this contract may be required to assign to us rights of recovery against another party, up to the amount we have paid. The covered party must do nothing after loss to impair those rights.

The employee must give notice as soon as practicable, protect the property from further damage, keep an accurate record of repair expenses, and produce receipts, inventories and other records that we reasonably request. A sworn proof of loss must be signed and delivered within 90 days after our request. These duties are conditions precedent to payment.
4.7. Appraisal. If the parties fail to agree on the amount of loss, either may demand an appraisal. Each party selects a competent appraiser within 30 days; the appraisers select an umpire. A decision agreed to by any two is binding. Each party pays its own appraiser and shares the cost of the umpire equally.
4.8. Nuclear hazard. We do not cover loss caused directly or indirectly by nuclear reaction, radiation or radioactive contamination, whether controlled or uncontrolled, and whether or not caused by a peril otherwise covered.
4.9. Cancellation. The employee may cancel at any time by returning the contract to us or by notifying us in writing of the date cancellation is to take effect. ======================================================================
SECTION 1 — PURPOSE AND SCOPE
======================================================================
This policy sets out when Saltmarsh Industries reimburses relocation costs for employees who move at the company's request. It applies to all grades and locations.

======================================================================
SECTION 2 — RULES
======================================================================
1. Eligibility (distance test). A relocation is eligible only if the one-way distance from the employee's former home to the new workplace exceeds the distance from the former home to the former workplace by at least 50 km.
2. Time limit. Claims must be submitted with receipts within 90 days of the employee's start date at the new workplace. Where the employee is on approved leave during that period, the limit is extended by the number of leave days.
3. Caps. Reimbursement is capped by grade: G1 $3,000; G2 $6,000; G3 $12,000. Amounts above the cap are not reimbursed.
4. Dependants supplement. Where a spouse, partner or dependent child moves with the employee, the cap is increased by $1,000.
5. Excluded costs. Costs of buying or selling a home, mortgage penalties, and temporary accommodation beyond 30 nights are not reimbursable under this policy.
6. Repayment. An employee who leaves the company within 12 months of the start date must repay the reimbursement pro rata.

======================================================================
SECTION 3 — PROCESS
======================================================================
3.1. Receipts. Only itemised receipts in the employee's name are accepted. Credit-card statements alone are not sufficient. Receipts in a foreign currency are converted at the company's monthly rate for the month of the expense.
3.2. Advances. An advance of up to 50% of the applicable cap may be requested before the move; it is deducted from the final reimbursement. Unused advances must be repaid within 20 days.
3.3. Audit. Internal audit samples 10% of relocation claims each year. A claim found to be inaccurate may be recovered from salary in accordance with the deductions policy.
3.4. Interaction with other policies. Travel on the move day is reimbursed under this policy, not under the travel policy. Costs reimbursed under this policy are not claimable again under any other policy.
3.5. Approvals. A relocation must be approved in writing by the receiving manager and by HR (Corin Haldane's team) before the move date. Approval is recorded on form RL-96 and attached to the employee's file.
3.6. Definitions. 'Start date' means the first day the employee is required to attend the new workplace, as stated in the transfer letter. 'Former home' means the address on file on the date of the transfer letter.
3.7. Temporary accommodation. Where temporary accommodation is reimbursed, the employee must move to permanent accommodation within 30 nights; extensions require the approval of the HR director.
3.8. Tax treatment. Reimbursements are reported in accordance with local tax rules. Where a reimbursement is taxable, the amount paid to the employee is not grossed up unless the offer letter says otherwise.

======================================================================
SECTION 4 — GENERAL PROVISIONS
======================================================================
4.1. Nuclear hazard. We do not cover loss caused directly or indirectly by nuclear reaction, radiation or radioactive contamination, whether controlled or uncontrolled, and whether or not caused by a peril otherwise covered.
4.2. Duties after loss. The employee must give notice as soon as practicable, protect the property from further damage, keep an accurate record of repair expenses, and produce receipts, inventories and other records that we reasonably request. A sworn proof of loss must be signed and delivered within 30 days after our request. These duties are conditions precedent to payment.
4.3. Mortgagee clause. If a mortgagee is named in the declarations, any loss payable under Coverage A is paid to the mortgagee and the employee as interests appear. Denial of the employee's claim does not apply to a valid claim of the mortgagee if the mortgagee notifies us of any change in ownership, occupancy or substantial change in risk of which it is aware.
4.4. Salvage. When we pay for a loss we may take all or part of the damaged property at an agreed or appraised value. There is no abandonment of property to us.
4.5. Assignment. Assignment of this contract is not valid unless we give our written consent.
4.6. Intentional loss. We do not cover loss caused by an act that the employee committed, or directed someone else to commit, intending the loss to happen.
4.7. Cancellation. The employee may cancel at any time by returning the contract to us or by notifying us in writing of the date cancellation is to take effect. We may cancel by mailing notice at least 10 days before the effective date, or 30 days where the cancellation is for reasons other than non-payment. Unearned premium is refunded pro rata.
4.8. Governmental action. We do not cover the destruction, confiscation or seizure of property by order of any governmental or public authority, except as ordered to prevent the spread of fire.

======================================================================
SECTION 5 — AMENDMENTS
======================================================================
AMENDMENT A-70 (effective 11 July 2026): for relocations where the employee's start date at the new workplace is on or after the effective date, the caps in rule 3 are increased to G1 $4,500; G2 $7,500; G3 $13,500. Relocations with earlier start dates remain on the previous caps.

======================================================================

======================================================================

Distances (from the former home, one way, per the routing tool): to former workplace 18 km; to new workplace 30 km.

question.instructions: How many exclusions bar cover for the building water damage in claim CLM-4270852, after applying any exceptions?

rationale: (1) The dwelling was without furnishings and empty for 44 days (not more than 45), so it was neither vacant nor unoccupied under the definitions. (2) The vacancy exclusion does not apply. (6) Decision: pay, subject to the $10,000 sublimit ($23,000 - $500 = $22,500, capped at $10,000 = $10,000). (7) Exclusions barring cover with no exception: 0.

======================================================================
SECTION 1 — PURPOSE AND SCOPE
======================================================================
This policy sets out when Driftwood Industries reimburses relocation costs for employees who move at the company's request. It applies to all grades and locations.

======================================================================
SECTION 2 — RULES
======================================================================
1. Eligibility (distance test). A relocation is eligible only if the one-way distance from the employee's former home to the new workplace exceeds the distance from the former home to the former workplace by at least 40 km.
2. Time limit. Claims must be submitted with receipts within 90 days of the employee's start date at the new workplace. Where the employee is on approved leave during that period, the limit is extended by the number of leave days.
3. Caps. Reimbursement is capped by grade: G1 $3,000; G2 $6,000; G3 $12,000. Amounts above the cap are not reimbursed.
4. Dependants supplement. Where a spouse, partner or dependent child moves with the employee, the cap is increased by $2,000.
5. Excluded costs. Costs of buying or selling a home, mortgage penalties, and temporary accommodation beyond 30 nights are not reimbursable under this policy.
6. Repayment. An employee who leaves the company within 12 months of the start date must repay the reimbursement pro rata.

======================================================================
SECTION 3 — PROCESS
======================================================================
3.1. Data protection. Documents submitted with a claim are kept for 7 years after the claim is closed and are accessible only to HR and to the auditors.
3.2. Receipts. Only itemised receipts in the employee's name are accepted. Credit-card statements alone are not sufficient. Receipts in a foreign currency are converted at the company's monthly rate for the month of the expense.
3.3. Approvals. A relocation must be approved in writing by the receiving manager and by HR (Kalinda Iversen's team) before the move date. Approval is recorded on form RL-87 and attached to the employee's file.
3.4. Advances. An advance of up to 50% of the applicable cap may be requested before the move; it is deducted from the final reimbursement. Unused advances must be repaid within 45 days.
3.5. Appeals. An employee may appeal a decision under this policy within 5 business days by writing to the HR director. The appeal is decided within 45 days; the decision on appeal is final.
3.6. Definitions. 'Start date' means the first day the employee is required to attend the new workplace, as stated in the transfer letter. 'Former home' means the address on file on the date of the transfer letter.
3.7. Interaction with other policies. Travel on the move day is reimbursed under this policy, not under the travel policy. Costs reimbursed under this policy are not claimable again under any other policy.

======================================================================
SECTION 4 — GENERAL PROVISIONS
======================================================================
4.1. Intentional loss. We do not cover loss caused by an act that the employee committed, or directed someone else to commit, intending the loss to happen.
4.2. Recovered property. If the employee or we recover any property for which we have made payment, the employee must notify us. The property may be returned to the employee, in which case the loss payment is adjusted accordingly.
4.3. Loss payment. We will adjust all losses with the employee and pay within 30 days after we reach agreement, after entry of a final judgment, or after the filing of an appraisal award with us, whichever comes first.
4.4. Duties after loss. The employee must give notice as soon as practicable, protect the property from further damage, keep an accurate record of repair expenses, and produce receipts, inventories and other records that we reasonably request. A sworn proof of loss must be signed and delivered within 30 days after our request. These duties are conditions precedent to payment.
4.5. Territorial limits. Coverage applies to losses occurring within the territory shown in the declarations. Property temporarily removed from the premises is covered for up to 15% of the applicable limit, but not for more than 30 consecutive days.
4.6. Electronic data. Loss of or damage to electronic data is covered only for the cost of blank media and the cost of copying from backups, subject to a limit of $2,500 per occurrence.
4.7. Nuclear hazard. We do not cover loss caused directly or indirectly by nuclear reaction, radiation or radioactive contamination, whether controlled or uncontrolled, and whether or not caused by a peril otherwise covered.
4.8. Neglect. We do not cover loss that results from the employee failing to take reasonable steps to protect and preserve the property once a loss has occurred.
4.9. Waiver or change of provisions. A waiver or change of a provision of this contract must be in writing by us to be valid. Our request for an appraisal or examination does not waive any of our rights.

======================================================================
SECTION 5 — AMENDMENTS
======================================================================
AMENDMENT A-25 (effective 11 August 2025): for relocations where the employee's start date at the new workplace is on or after the effective date, the caps in rule 3 are increased to G1 $4,000; G2 $7,000; G3 $13,000. Relocations with earlier start dates remain on the previous caps.

======================================================================
SECTION 6 — CASE FILE REL-140031
======================================================================
Case REL-140031. Employee: Rosa Zubair (EMP-83390), grade G2. Former workplace: Nairobi office. New workplace: Mexico City plant. Start date at new workplace: 10 September 2025.
Distances (from the former home, one way, per the routing tool): to former workplace 37 km; to new workplace 49 km.

======================================================================
SECTION 1 — PURPOSE AND SCOPE
======================================================================
This policy sets out when Cinder Energy reimburses relocation costs for employees who move at the company's request. It applies to all grades and locations.

======================================================================
SECTION 2 — RULES
======================================================================
1. Eligibility (distance test). A relocation is eligible only if the one-way distance from the employee's former home to the new workplace exceeds the distance from the former home to the former workplace by at least 50 km.
2. Time limit. Claims must be submitted with receipts within 120 days of the employee's start date at the new workplace. Where the employee is on approved leave during that period, the limit is extended by the number of leave days.
3. Caps. Reimbursement is capped by grade: G1 $3,000; G2 $7,500; G3 $12,000. Amounts above the cap are not reimbursed.
4. Dependants supplement. Where a spouse, partner or dependent child moves with the employee, the cap is increased by $2,000.
5. Excluded costs. Costs of buying or selling a home, mortgage penalties, and temporary accommodation beyond 30 nights are not reimbursable under this policy.
6. Repayment. An employee who leaves the company within 12 months of the start date must repay the reimbursement pro rata.

======================================================================

This policy sets out when Halcyon Technologies reimburses relocation costs for employees who move at the company's request. It applies to all grades and locations.

======================================================================
SECTION 2 — RULES
======================================================================
1. Eligibility (distance test). A relocation is eligible only if the one-way distance from the employee's former home to the new workplace exceeds the distance from the former home to the former workplace by at least 80 km.
2. Time limit. Claims must be submitted with receipts within 90 days of the employee's start date at the new workplace. Where the employee is on approved leave during that period, the limit is extended by the number of leave days.
3. Caps. Reimbursement is capped by grade: G1 $4,000; G2 $6,000; G3 $10,000. Amounts above the cap are not reimbursed.
4. Dependants supplement. Where a spouse, partner or dependent child moves with the employee, the cap is increased by $1,500.
5. Excluded costs. Costs of buying or selling a home, mortgage penalties, and temporary accommodation beyond 30 nights are not reimbursable under this policy.
6. Repayment. An employee who leaves the company within 12 months of the start date must repay the reimbursement pro rata.

======================================================================
SECTION 3 — PROCESS
======================================================================
3.1. Approvals. A relocation must be approved in writing by the receiving manager and by HR (Katja Lindqvist's team) before the move date. Approval is recorded on form RL-98 and attached to the employee's file.
3.2. Data protection. Documents submitted with a claim are kept for 7 years after the claim is closed and are accessible only to HR and to the auditors.
3.3. Definitions. 'Start date' means the first day the employee is required to attend the new workplace, as stated in the transfer letter. 'Former home' means the address on file on the date of the transfer letter.
3.4. Audit. Internal audit samples 10% of relocation claims each year. A claim found to be inaccurate may be recovered from salary in accordance with the deductions policy.
3.5. Interaction with other policies. Travel on the move day is reimbursed under this policy, not under the travel policy. Costs reimbursed under this policy are not claimable again under any other policy.
3.6. Appeals. An employee may appeal a decision under this policy within 15 business days by writing to the HR director. The appeal is decided within 30 days; the decision on appeal is final.
3.7. Temporary accommodation. Where temporary accommodation is reimbursed, the employee must move to permanent accommodation within 30 nights; extensions require the approval of the HR director.
3.8. Tax treatment. Reimbursements are reported in accordance with local tax rules. Where a reimbursement is taxable, the amount paid to the employee is not grossed up unless the offer letter says otherwise.
3.9. Receipts. Only itemised receipts in the employee's name are accepted. Credit-card statements alone are not sufficient. Receipts in a foreign currency are converted at the company's monthly rate for the month of the expense.

======================================================================
SECTION 4 — GENERAL PROVISIONS
======================================================================
4.1. Nuclear hazard. We do not cover loss caused directly or indirectly by nuclear reaction, radiation or radioactive contamination, whether controlled or uncontrolled, and whether or not caused by a peril otherwise covered.
4.2. Other insurance. If a loss covered by this contract is also covered by other insurance, we will pay only the proportion of the loss that the limit of liability that applies under this contract bears to the total amount of insurance covering the loss.
4.3. Waiver or change of provisions. A waiver or change of a provision of this contract must be in writing by us to be valid. Our request for an appraisal or examination does not waive any of our rights.
4.4. Inflation guard. The limits shown in the declarations increase by 4% at each anniversary of the inception date unless this endorsement is deleted by the employee.
4.5. Ordinance or law. Extra cost caused by having to comply with building codes or other regulations when repairing, rebuilding or demolishing is covered up to 15% of the Coverage A limit.
4.6. Territorial limits. Coverage applies to losses occurring within the territory shown in the declarations. Property temporarily removed from the premises is covered for up to 15% of the applicable limit, but not for more than 30 consecutive days.
4.7. Neglect. We do not cover loss that results from the employee failing to take reasonable steps to protect and preserve the property once a loss has occurred.
4.8. Definitions of general application. In this contract 'we' and 'us' mean the insurer that issued it, and 'you' means the employee shown on the declarations page. 'Business day' means a day other than Saturday, Sunday or a public holiday at the place shown in the declarations.
4.9. Mortgagee clause. If a mortgagee is named in the declarations, any loss payable under Coverage A is paid to the mortgagee and the employee as interests appear. Denial of the employee's claim does not apply to a valid claim of the mortgagee if the mortgagee notifies us of any change in ownership, occupancy or substantial change in risk of which it is aware.
4.10. Cancellation. The employee may cancel at any time by returning the contract to us or by notifying us in writing of the date cancellation is to take effect. We may cancel by mailing notice at least 30 days before the effective date, or 90 days where the cancellation is for reasons other than non-payment. Unearned premium is refunded pro rata.

======================================================================
SECTION 5 — AMENDMENTS
======================================================================
AMENDMENT A-82 (effective 20 February 2026): for relocations where the employee's start date at the new workplace is on or after the effective date, the caps in rule 3 are increased to G1 $5,500; G2 $7,500; G3 $11,500. Relocations with earlier start dates remain on the previous caps.

======================================================================
SECTION 1 — PURPOSE AND SCOPE

This policy sets out when Westmark Systems reimburses relocation costs for employees who move at the company's request. It applies to all grades and locations.

======================================================================

1. Eligibility (distance test). A relocation is eligible only if the one-way distance from the employee's former home to the new workplace exceeds the distance from the former home to the former workplace by at least 60 km.
2. Time limit. Claims must be submitted with receipts within 60 days of the employee's start date at the new workplace. Where the employee is on approved leave during that period, the limit is extended by the number of leave days.
3. Caps. Reimbursement is capped by grade: G1 $4,000; G2 $7,500; G3 $10,000. Amounts above the cap are not reimbursed.
4. Dependants supplement. Where a spouse, partner or dependent child moves with the employee, the cap is increased by $2,000.
5. Excluded costs. Costs of buying or selling a home, mortgage penalties, and temporary accommodation beyond 30 nights are not reimbursable under this policy.
6. Repayment. An employee who leaves the company within 12 months of the start date must repay the reimbursement pro rata.

======================================================================
SECTION 3 — PROCESS
======================================================================
3.1. Temporary accommodation. Where temporary accommodation is reimbursed, the employee must move to permanent accommodation within 30 nights; extensions require the approval of the HR director.
3.2. Approvals. A relocation must be approved in writing by the receiving manager and by HR (Leif Nowicki's team) before the move date. Approval is recorded on form RL-31 and attached to the employee's file.
3.3. Receipts. Only itemised receipts in the employee's name are accepted. Credit-card statements alone are not sufficient. Receipts in a foreign currency are converted at the company's monthly rate for the month of the expense.
3.4. Appeals. An employee may appeal a decision under this policy within 10 business days by writing to the HR director. The appeal is decided within 30 days; the decision on appeal is final.
3.5. Tax treatment. Reimbursements are reported in accordance with local tax rules. Where a reimbursement is taxable, the amount paid to the employee is not grossed up unless the offer letter says otherwise.
3.6. Definitions. 'Start date' means the first day the employee is required to attend the new workplace, as stated in the transfer letter. 'Former home' means the address on file on the date of the transfer letter.
3.7. Audit. Internal audit samples 10% of relocation claims each year. A claim found to be inaccurate may be recovered from salary in accordance with the deductions policy.

======================================================================
SECTION 4 — GENERAL PROVISIONS
======================================================================
4.1. Appraisal. If the parties fail to agree on the amount of loss, either may demand an appraisal. Each party selects a competent appraiser within 10 days; the appraisers select an umpire. A decision agreed to by any two is binding. Each party pays its own appraiser and shares the cost of the umpire equally.
4.2. Waiver or change of provisions. A waiver or change of a provision of this contract must be in writing by us to be valid. Our request for an appraisal or examination does not waive any of our rights.
4.3. Intentional loss. We do not cover loss caused by an act that the employee committed, or directed someone else to commit, intending the loss to happen.
4.4. Governmental action. We do not cover the destruction, confiscation or seizure of property by order of any governmental or public authority, except as ordered to prevent the spread of fire.
4.5. Volunteer payments. We will not pay for any expense voluntarily incurred by the employee beyond $1,000 without our prior agreement, except for emergency measures reasonably necessary to protect the property from further loss.
4.6. Concealment or fraud. We do not provide coverage if, whether before or after a loss, the employee has intentionally concealed or misrepresented any material fact or circumstance, engaged in fraudulent conduct, or made false statements relating to this contract.
4.7. Salvage. When we pay for a loss we may take all or part of the damaged property at an agreed or appraised value. There is no abandonment of property to us.
4.8. Ordinance or law. Extra cost caused by having to comply with building codes or other regulations when repairing, rebuilding or demolishing is covered up to 10% of the Coverage A limit.
4.9. Other insurance. If a loss covered by this contract is also covered by other insurance, we will pay only the proportion of the loss that the limit of liability that applies under this contract bears to the total amount of insurance covering the loss.
4.10. Cancellation. The employee may cancel at any time by returning the contract to us or by notifying us in writing of the date cancellation is to take effect. We may cancel by mailing notice at least 10 days before the effective date, or 60 days where the cancellation is for reasons other than non-payment. Unearned premium is refunded pro rata.

======================================================================
1. Eligibility (distance test). A relocation is eligible only if the one-way distance from the employee's former home to the new workplace exceeds the distance from the former home to the former workplace by at least 40 km.

3. Caps. Reimbursement is capped by grade: G1 $3,000; G2 $7,500; G3 $10,000. Amounts above the cap are not reimbursed.
4. Dependants supplement. Where a spouse, partner or dependent child moves with the employee, the cap is increased by $1,500.
5. Excluded costs. Costs of buying or selling a home, mortgage penalties, and temporary accommodation beyond 30 nights are not reimbursable under this policy.
6. Repayment. An employee who leaves the company within 12 months of the start date must repay the reimbursement pro rata.

======================================================================

======================================================================
3.1. Definitions. 'Start date' means the first day the employee is required to attend the new workplace, as stated in the transfer letter. 'Former home' means the address on file on the date of the transfer letter.
3.2. Temporary accommodation. Where temporary accommodation is reimbursed, the employee must move to permanent accommodation within 30 nights; extensions require the approval of the HR director.
3.3. Receipts. Only itemised receipts in the employee's name are accepted. Credit-card statements alone are not sufficient. Receipts in a foreign currency are converted at the company's monthly rate for the month of the expense.
3.4. Interaction with other policies. Travel on the move day is reimbursed under this policy, not under the travel policy. Costs reimbursed under this policy are not claimable again under any other policy.
3.5. Audit. Internal audit samples 10% of relocation claims each year. A claim found to be inaccurate may be recovered from salary in accordance with the deductions policy.
3.6. Data protection. Documents submitted with a claim are kept for 5 years after the claim is closed and are accessible only to HR and to the auditors.
3.7. Approvals. A relocation must be approved in writing by the receiving manager and by HR (Cerys Tremblay's team) before the move date. Approval is recorded on form RL-49 and attached to the employee's file.

======================================================================
4.1. Volunteer payments. We will not pay for any expense voluntarily incurred by the employee beyond $500 without our prior agreement, except for emergency measures reasonably necessary to protect the property from further loss.
